questions.q: Who built and consecrated the Sheep Gate?
questions.a: Eliashib built and consecrated the Sheep Gate along with his brothers, the priests.
The sons of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate.

questions.q: Whose nobles refused to do the work ordered by their lords?
questions.a: The nobles of the Tekoites refused to do the work.
Joiada and Meshullam repaired the Old Gate.

questions.q: Who repaired Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall?
questions.a: Uzziel and Hananiah repaired that portion of Jerusalem.

questions.q: Who repaired another section along with the Tower of Ovens?
questions.a: Malkijah (the son of Harim) and Hasshub repaired another section and the Tower of Ovens.

questions.q: Who helped Shallum repair the walls?
Who repaired the Valley Gate as far as the Dung Gate?
questions.a: Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate and the entire portion of wall between the Valley Gate and the Dung Gate.
Malkijah (the son of Recab) repaired the Dung Gate.

questions.q: Who repaired the Fountain Gate and the wall of the Pool of Siloam?
questions.a: Shallun repaired the Fountain Gate and the wall of the Pool of Siloam.

questions.q: Who repaired from the place across from the tombs of David to the house of the mighty men?
questions.a: Nehemiah the son of Azbuk repaired that section.

questions.q: Who repaired from the angle to the door of the house of Elisahib the high priest?
Which section of the wall did Benjamin and Hasshub repair?
questions.a: They repaired the section in front of their own house.

questions.q: Who did the repairs on the section above the Horse Gate?
questions.a: The priests repaired that section. Each of the priests repaired in front of his own house.

questions.q: Who repaired the wall between the upper changes of the corner and the Sheep Gate?
questions.a: The goldsmiths and the merchants repaired that section.

commentary.text: The rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem.

—The work was divided, so that every one might know what he had to do, and mind it, with a desire to excel; yet without contention, or separate interests. No strife appears among them, but which should do most for the public good. Every Israelite should lend a hand toward the building up of Jerusalem. Let not nobles think any thing below them, by which they may advance the good of their country. Even some females helped forward the work. Some repaired over against their houses, and one repaired over against his chamber. When a general good work is to be done, each should apply himself to that part which is within his reach. If every one will sweep before his own door, the street will be clean; if every one will mend one, we shall all be mended. Some that had first done helped their fellows. The walls of Jerusalem, in heaps of rubbish, represent the desperate state of the world around, while the number and malice of those who hindered the building, give some faint idea of the enemies we have to contend with, while executing the work of God. Every one must begin at home; for it is by getting the work of God advanced in our own souls that we shall best contribute to the good of the church of Christ. May the Lord thus stir up the hearts of his people, to lay aside their petty disputes, and to disregard their worldly interests, compared with building the walls of Jerusalem, and defending the cause of truth and godliness against the assaults of avowed enemies.
